question_text: What do you understand by 'self inductance'?

mark_split.label: The emf form and the unit

Physics hand-checked: NΦ = L i defines L as flux linkage per unit current in the same coil; ε = −L di/dt; SI unit henry, 1 H = 1 V per (A s⁻¹).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
steps.mark_note: L = flux linkage per unit current
lines: When the current in a coil changes, the
flux linked with the coil changes, so an
emf is induced in the same coil. This is
The flux linkage is proportional to the
L is called the self inductance of the
coil — its flux linkage per unit current.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The coil's OWN current makes its own flux linkage; L is the ratio of the two.
steps.why: The definition ties L to the coil itself: its own changing current, its own flux. That is what the word self records.
common_mistakes: Defining L with two coils. Flux from the coil's OWN current defines self inductance; two coils give mutual inductance.

recall.must_convey: That self inductance is the flux linkage of a coil per unit current flowing in the same coil.

steps.memory_tip: Self = same coil twice: its own current makes its own flux linkage, and L is the ratio.

steps.label: The emf form and the unit
lines: The emf induced in the coil is
So L is numerically the emf induced when
the current changes at the rate 1 A s⁻¹.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The emf form with its minus sign, and the unit henry.
steps.why: The emf form is the definition in action: it makes L measurable, as the emf per unit rate of change of current.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign in ε = −L di/dt. The sign is Lenz's law and stays.
Writing the unit as weber. The weber is the unit of flux; flux linkage per ampere is the henry.

recall.must_convey: That the induced emf is minus L di by dt and the SI unit of L is the henry.
accept: minus L d i by d t
emf per unit rate of change of current

steps.memory_tip: Henry for inductance, weber for flux. One henry = one volt per ampere per second.

insider_note: Both marks live in the two equations: NΦ = L i for the definition, ε = −L di/dt with the unit henry for the second.
